worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=3$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+2\cdot 3\cdot \pi )=\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+6\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\sqrt{2},$ then $\operatorname{sec}⁡(x+6\pi )=\sqrt{2}.$
